name: DAAD EPOS - Development-Related Postgraduate Courses
requiredDocuments: Completed and signed DAAD application form(s) (you may apply for up to three EPOS-listed courses; list them in order of priority)
Curriculum vitae in reverse chronological order without unexplained gaps (Europass template), with exact information about studies and practical experience

One Letter of Motivation with detailed academic, professional and personal reasons for applying (if applying to more than one course, justify the choice and prioritisation of courses in a single uniform letter)
Letter of recommendation from your current employer (official letterhead, signature, official stamp, current date, not in a sealed envelope)

Certificate(s) of Employment proving at least two years of relevant work experience after the Bachelor's degree up to the time of application (ideally including a guarantee of re-employment on return home)
Recent proof of language skills: English (IELTS or TOEFL — institutional TOEFL not accepted) or German (required for German-taught courses)
Copies of higher-education degree certificates (certified translation if not in German or English)
Copy of full set of transcript of records (with an explanation of the grading system if not included)
APS Certificate (required only for applicants from the People's Republic of China)

timeline.deadline: Varies by chosen EPOS-listed course (no single global deadline). Example: MIDE at HTW Berlin closes 31 August 2025 for a 1 April 2026 start.
timeline.notes: EPOS has no single DAAD deadline — you apply directly to the master's course and each course sets its own deadline (see the official 'List of all Postgraduate courses with application deadlines 2027/28' PDF). The DAAD selection process for all listed courses runs from end of October to March. As of 2026-06 the documented cycle is the 2026/2027 academic year from the official EPOS programme brochure; the deadlines list referenced on the page covers 2027/28 courses. Always check the individual course website/brochure for the exact, current deadline.

benefits: Monthly stipend of 992 EUR for graduate (master's) scholarship holders (1,300 EUR, rising to 1,400 EUR from February 2026, for doctoral candidates)
Payments towards health, accident and personal-liability insurance cover
Travel allowance, unless covered by the home country or another funding source
Possible monthly rent subsidy (under certain circumstances)
Possible monthly allowance for accompanying family members (under certain circumstances)
Tuition exemption/waiver at EPOS-listed courses for DAAD scholarship holders (handled per course)
For German-taught courses, an included preparatory German language course (2-6 months) in Germany before the study course begins
mustKnow: You apply DIRECTLY to a specific EPOS-listed master's course, NOT to the DAAD. Applications sent to the DAAD are not forwarded. You may apply to up to three courses, ranked by priority.

Two-step process: (1) apply to the course; (2) a selection committee proposes candidates; (3) DAAD then invites the proposed candidates to upload their complete documents to the DAAD Portal; (4) final selection. Keep PDF copies of every document ready for the portal upload.
Work-experience gate: you need a Bachelor's degree (usually a four-year course) PLUS at least two years of relevant professional experience after the Bachelor's, up to the application deadline.
Recency rule: academic degrees should normally be no more than six years old at the time of application.
Residency exclusion: applicants who have lived in Germany for longer than 15 months at the application deadline cannot be considered.

Nationality gate: open only to nationals on the OECD-DAC developing-country list supported by EPOS (Bangladesh is included — confirmed under 'South and Central Asia' in the official DAC list, validity 2024-2025); a few DAC countries are explicitly excluded (Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia incl. Kosovo, Turkey).
Development-related motivation is assessed: typical holders work in a public authority or a state/private company in a developing country on development-policy planning/projects.
Funded by Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ); scholarship announcement depends on BMZ funds being provided.
Fully funded with a living stipend (not tuition-only): stipend + insurance + travel, with tuition exempted/waived per EPOS course for DAAD scholars.

universities: Selected German state or state-recognised universities and universities of applied sciences offering EPOS-listed postgraduate courses (e.g. Universität Leipzig, Universität Stuttgart, Heidelberg, HTW Berlin, MIPLC Munich)

duration: 12 to 42 months depending on the study programme (12-24 months for a master's degree; 40-42 months for a PhD)
intake: Academic year 2026/2027 (intake date set by each EPOS-listed course; e.g. MIDE/HTW Berlin begins 1 April 2026)
eligibleNationalities: Open to graduates from countries on the OECD-DAC developing/newly-industrialised country list supported in the EPOS programme. Bangladesh is included (listed under 'South and Central Asia' in the official DAC list, validity 2024-2025). Excluded DAC countries: Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia (including Kosovo) and Turkey. Applicants resident in Germany longer than 15 months at the deadline are not eligible.
languageRequirements: For English-taught courses: proof of adequate English per the course's regulations (IELTS or TOEFL; institutional TOEFL not accepted). For German-taught courses: DSH 2 or TestDaF 4 before the course starts, with at least German B1 at application (proven by certificate); a 6-month intensive German course in Germany is included but cannot replace prior B1 knowledge.
ageLimit: No fixed age limit, but academic degrees should normally be no more than six years old at the time of application.
applicationFee: No DAAD application fee mentioned; apply directly to the course (course/admission or language-test fees, if any, are separate and not specified by DAAD).
monthlyStipend: 992 EUR per month for graduate (master's) scholarship holders
renewalConditions: Funding runs for the duration of the study programme (12-42 months) contingent on satisfactory academic progress; for German-taught courses, passing DSH 2 / TestDaF 4 is a formal prerequisite for university matriculation.
postStudyWork: Programme expects graduates to return to and apply their skills in their home country/region (development-related objective); a guarantee of re-employment from the current employer is requested where possible.
